articles.title: From mass detentions to political war of words: How Delhi protests unfolded
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi witnessed an extraordinary security clampdown on October 10 as police moved to prevent the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi witnessed an extraordinary security clampdown on October 10 as police moved to prevent the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. What began with barricades, transport restrictions and preventive detentions escalated into a day of mass arrests, street demonstrations, reported clashes and a fierce political confrontation over the right to protest.Delhi Police detained (and later released barring CJP leaders) more than 7,000 people across the national capital. Those detained included CJP leaders, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, student activists, lawyers and other opposition leaders. Two police personnel were reported injured in incidents involving stone-pelting.As the detentions mounted, opposition leaders accused the government of suppressing dissent. BJP defended the police action and the SIR process, accusing the protesters of attempting to create unrest.CJP later announced to continue the agitation as it vowed to march again to Jantar Mantar on Sunday.Here is how the day unfolded for protesters, from the security measures before sunrise to the political confrontation that followed.Early morning: Delhi tightens security, detentions beginDelhi Police denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing procedural lapses and law-and-order concerns. Authorities planned to deploy around 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel, with barricades, checkpoints, metro restrictions and mobile internet curbs in parts of central Delhi. Services to and from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations were expected to be particularly affected.Police personnel wearing body cameras and drones were deployed for surveillance.Police also detained 30–40 people with criminal records as a preventive measure. At least 600 people had been detained across Delhi by 9am.Morning: CJP leaders and Dhruv Rathee detainedCJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained inside an aircraft shortly after it landed in Delhi from Mumbai. CJP called the action pre-planned and demanded their immediate release.YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was also detained from his Gurugram residence. CJP accused the government of targeting young people who questioned its actions.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh and content creator Kavya Karnatac were also reported detained. CJP later alleged that Ratna Singh was being held inside a car surrounded by around 35 police personnel and the deputy commissioner of police. Police also placed several Congress workers and members of other political parties under house arrest ahead of the demonstration.Meanwhile, BJP president Nitin Nabin accused Rahul Gandhi and CJP associates of attempting to destabilise the country for political gains, alleging that their actions were driven by foreign forces.Late morning: Students, lawyers and activists detainedMore than 400 SFI members, other student activists and lawyers marching from the Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were detained. SFI and Left party workers staged protests at INA and near the BJP headquarters as the protest crackdown continued.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan was also reported detained.Student leader Neha Bora, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, and activist Prashant Bhushan and Yogendra Yadav were among those detained near INA market while heading towards the protest. Bora had led a march from Jor Bagh towards Dilli Haat-INA.CJP named Ajinkya Shinde to lead the protest in a pre-recorded video. Following the announcement, Ajinkya urged protesters to turn any location where police stopped them into their “Jantar Mantar”.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor described the situation as an “undeclared Emer-GenZ”. He criticised the heavy security deployment, train cancellations, metro closures and restrictions on movement.Afternoon: Kejriwal and Mamata detainedFormer Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee were detained while heading to join the protest. Mamata said they had been taken around in a prisoner van for two hours. She announced a sit-in at Dwarka North police station and said she would join the INDIA march on Monday.Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi criticised the crackdown ahead of the planned protest. Kharge accused the Modi government of suppressing dissent, saying it had turned the “mother of democracy” into a "muzzled democracy”. Meanwhile, Priyanka alleged that the government had curtailed constitutional rights.Police officials reported stones being pelted at a bus carrying detained protesters in Jhandewalan. Two police personnel, including a Pink Force member, were reported injured. Another officer was injured in alleged stone-pelting near Baba Kharak Singh Marg in Connaught Place, where police said a scuffle broke out as they tried to disperse protesters.By late afternoon, the reported detention count had risen from at least 600 in the morning to around 1,000 by afternoon.BJP defends SIR, criticises oppositionBJP spokesperson Sambit Patra accused Rahul Gandhi of attempting to drag the President into a street protest. The party defended the police action, describing it as a victory for democracy over “mob rule”. Nabin had earlier accused the protesters of trying to destabilise the country.Court intervention and challenges to restrictionsChief Justice of India Surya Kant communicated to authorities that lawyers detained while peacefully protesting outside the Supreme Court should be released. The intervention followed an urgent letter from the Supreme Court Bar Association, which said several advocates had been taken to the Yamuna Sports Complex.CPM general secretary MA Baby filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging restrictions imposed ahead of the protest, including curbs on metro services and mobile internet connectivity. TMC spokesperson Saket Gokhale also wrote to the Delhi high court’s acting chief justice, seeking suo motu intervention over the transport restrictions.Evening: Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi sharpen attackRahul Gandhi targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and national security adviser Ajit Doval. He accused them of attacking the Constitution and vowed to continue the fight to defend democratic rights. Mamata Banerjee said she would remain in Delhi and join the INDIA march on Monday, in protest against the treatment of young people and other protesters.Meanwhile, an open letter signed by 124 former IAS and IFS officers strongly defended the Election Commission and the SIR process, adding to the debate over the electoral-roll revision.CJP vows to return to Jantar MantarCJP in a press conference announced to march to Jantar Mantar again on Sunday.It said they will "not back down until demands are met" after mass detentions and alleged the Modi government feared that a united opposition could threaten its hold on power.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Saturday held that student activist Sharjeel Imam, accused in the 2020 northeast Delhi riots larger conspiracy case, "apparently flouted" an interim bail condition by coming into contact with the media. articles.title: After a 2015 flash flood shut Death Valley’s Scotty’s Castle, visitors can return from October 10 for limited guided exterior tours while restoration of the historic estate continues
articles.summary: More than a decade after a devastating flash flood forced one of Death Valley National Park’s best-known historic sites to close, visitors are getting
articles.body: More than a decade after a devastating flash flood forced one of Death Valley National Park’s best-known historic sites to close, visitors are getting another chance to see Scotty’s Castle. The National Park Service is offering limited guided exterior tours of the historic estate beginning October 10. Tours are scheduled for most Saturdays and Sundays through April 17, while private weekday tours can also be arranged for small groups. The castle itself remains under restoration and is not yet reopening for regular interior visits.The limited access marks another step in a recovery effort that has stretched for more than 10 years and is expected to continue for at least another two.A 2015 flood changed everything at Scotty’s CastleScotty’s Castle has been closed since October 2015, when an extraordinary storm hit the northern part of Death Valley.On October 18, the area received 2.75 inches of rain in about five hours, roughly equivalent to a typical year’s rainfall there. Another half-inch had fallen the previous day. Water, mud and rocks rushed through Grapevine Canyon in a flash flood estimated to be flowing at about 3,200 cubic feet per second.The flood damaged buildings, utilities, historic landscaping and roads. Much of the eight-mile Bonnie Clare Road leading toward Scotty’s Castle was destroyed. More than 20 power poles were washed away, sections of the water and sewer systems were damaged and mud and rocks piled several feet deep around some buildings.The National Park Service estimates that the overall repair effort costs about $71 million, with work divided across numerous projects and funding sources.Visitors can now see the historic grounds againThe new tours are limited to the exterior areas of the historic district while construction continues.National Park Service rangers and guides from the Death Valley Natural History Association will lead visitors through the site, explaining its history as well as the restoration work underway. Tickets are being handled through the association.The arrangement gives visitors access to one of Death Valley’s most recognizable historic landmarks without reopening sections that remain affected by construction and preservation work.It also allows the park to tell the story of the recovery itself, including how infrastructure has been rebuilt to withstand future flooding.Who actually built Scotty’s Castle?Despite its name, Scotty’s Castle was not built by Walter “Scotty” Scott.The Spanish Revival-style estate dates to the 1920s and was built by Chicago businessman Albert Johnson as a winter retreat for himself and his wife, Bessie. Scott was Johnson’s friend and became closely associated with the property through colorful stories that helped turn the desert estate into an attraction.Its unusual architecture and remote desert setting eventually made Scotty’s Castle one of Death Valley’s most distinctive historic sites.The property also contains historic furnishings, archives and museum objects connected to the people who lived and worked there.Restoration faced more than just the original floodRepairing the site has proved complicated.Beyond the extensive 2015 flood damage, restoration was affected by funding and contracting delays, the Covid-19 pandemic and later flooding elsewhere in Death Valley.Another major setback came in April 2021, when the historic Garage caught fire while repairs were underway. The building had been about 60% through its restoration when it was destroyed. The adjoining Longshed also suffered damage.Meanwhile, the park has rebuilt water, electrical and wastewater infrastructure and added new flood-control measures. Some of those improvements successfully protected the historic district when flooding associated with the remnants of Hurricane Hilary hit Death Valley in 2023.Full reopening could still be more than two years awayMore work is planned for 2027, including repairs to the parking lot, the historic Longshed and the Gas Tank House. The Gas Tank House is expected to be adapted into a small visitor contact station.Once construction is complete, curatorial teams will still need to return historic furniture and museum collections to the castle before regular interior tours can resume.Based on the current schedule, the National Park Service says November 2028 is the earliest anticipated date for a full reopening.Until then, the limited exterior tours offer visitors a rare opportunity to step back onto the grounds of a Death Valley landmark that has remained largely inaccessible since the flood of 2015.You use AI every day. articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Senior Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Saturday launched a sharp attack on the BJP government in Haryana, alleging that 70% of paddy procurement remained pending across the state's mandis. Addressing mediapersons alongside Thanesar MLA Ashok Arora at his residence, Hooda demanded a white paper on the state's claim of providing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 24 crops.Hooda highlighted that while paddy arrivals in mandis had touched 12 lakh metric tonnes, the government had procured only 30% of the crop. articles.title: Ben Affleck says he was banned from Instagram twice while monitoring his kids: The digital parenting dilemma
articles.summary: Ben Affleck tried to keep tabs on his children's social media accounts. Instagram's response? It banned him. Twice.
articles.body: Ben Affleck tried to keep tabs on his children's social media accounts. Instagram's response? It banned him. Twice.The Hollywood actor revealed that his attempts to monitor his children's online lives led to an unexpected problem: the platform flagged him for impersonating himself. His account had just six followers: his children and some of their friends and he had joined largely to see what they were doing online.“I got banned from Instagram twice for impersonating myself,” Affleck told Variety.It is an amusing twist, but behind it lies a dilemma familiar to parents everywhere. How do you protect children in a digital world that is constantly changing, especially when they may understand its platforms better than you do? And how do you keep them safe without making them feel that every corner of their lives is being watched?The problem is bigger than one parent's Instagram accountAffleck's experience also raises a question about the responsibility placed on parents.In a January 2026 report, The Guardian examined the AAP's updated approach to digital media. The report highlighted growing concern that screen-time limits alone cannot address the risks children face online.Adolescent psychologist Jessica Schleider told the publication that expecting parents to constantly monitor young people's digital activity can be unrealistic and, particularly for teenagers, potentially invasive.That does not mean parental involvement is unnecessary. Rather, it suggests that responsibility cannot rest entirely on families when the design of digital platforms also shapes children's experiences.Parents can establish rules, use available safety tools and help children recognise harmful behaviour. But they cannot be expected to watch every interaction or anticipate every risk.This is especially challenging when online trends, platform features and the ways young people communicate change faster than adults can keep up.Affleck's experience is funny because the situation is so unexpected: a famous actor, twice banned from a platform while trying to follow his own children. But it also captures a genuine difficulty. Parents are trying to understand a space that their children may already inhabit with greater ease.The real lesson is not to watch everythingThere is something reassuring about Affleck's admission. Despite his fame, he is not presenting himself as an expert on every corner of the internet. He is a parent trying to understand what his children experience online.His story does not tell us exactly how he manages their children's social media boundaries, and it would be unfair to draw conclusions about their private parenting arrangements from a brief anecdote.But it does capture a dilemma shared by many families: children need room to develop their own identities, while parents still have a responsibility to help them recognise danger and make informed choices.That balance is unlikely to be achieved through surveillance alone. It requires clear boundaries, honest conversations and a willingness to keep learning as children grow older.A parent may start by checking an Instagram account. The more difficult work is helping a child understand when to trust someone online, when to step away from a harmful interaction and when to ask for help.Affleck's six-follower account may have been an unusual way to approach the problem. Yet the concern behind it is ordinary.For parents raising children in the age of social media, the challenge is not simply finding a way to see everything their children do. It is building a relationship in which children feel safe enough to share what their parents cannot see.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Nepal cuts 12-yr wait to declare flood missing dead to 45 days
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nepal govt has reduced the waiting period for declaring people missing in disasters dead from 12 years to just 45 days, paving the way for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nepal govt has reduced the waiting period for declaring people missing in disasters dead from 12 years to just 45 days, paving the way for families of 5,285 people, including at least 189 Indians who went missing in the Aug 26 floods, to obtain death certificates and pursue compensation, insurance and inheritance claims. President Ram Chandra Poudel issued the ordinance late Friday, a day before the 45-day period since the disaster was due to end.The ordinance, issued on the recommendation of PM Balendra Shah's cabinet, took effect immediately. For families of the 189 missing Indians, the process begins with proof that their relatives were present in the flood-affected areas on Aug 26. Travel tickets, hotel bookings, employment records and last-known communications can serve as supporting evidence. Embassy of India in Kathmandu will coordinate with Nepalese authorities to verify the details, while local registration offices will process applications using nationality documents, police reports and embassy certification, where required.Once Nepalese authorities issue the death certificates and complete the necessary consular formalities, families can use the documents in India to pursue inheritance, insurance and other legal claims. Indian diplomatic officials and state administrations facilitate the cross-border documentation process.However, the ordinance did not establish whether foreign nationals would qualify for compensation under Nepal's disaster relief provisions.Foreign-issued death certificates are legally recognised in India for settling bank accounts, insurance, and property inheritance, provided they are properly authenticated — typically through an attestation by the Indian Embassy.The Aug 26 floods killed at least 1,455 people in Nepal, with authorities recovering as many bodies. Of them, only 112 have been identified and handed over to their families.In India, a person missing for at least seven years can be presumed dead. Following the 2013 Kedarnath floods, India introduced a special procedure allowing death registration after official verification without waiting seven years.Check out the six step process:Establish presence at flood site: Gather travel tickets, hotel bookings, phone records or last communications proving missing person was in affected area Contact Indian Embassy: Report disappearance to embassy of India in Kathmandu for coordination with Nepalese authorities and disaster victim identification systemApply under 45-day rule: Seek recognition of missing person's death under Nepal's new disaster ordinanceRegister death: After clearance from disaster management authorities, complete death registration at designated local ward office in NepalObtain consular certification: Secure death certificate, police reports and required attestations from Indian diplomatic authorities.Pursue claims in India: Submit death certificate and consular documents for insurance, bank settlements and inheritance claimsYou use AI every day. Addressing a public meeting in Balrampur, Adityanath invited Yadav to contest against him from the temple town, saying the two leaders should face each other directly.“Akhilesh ji, Ayodhya is our sacred abode. I visit Ayodhya repeatedly to ensure that there is no lapse in its development, and the identity of Uttar Pradesh is not tarnished in any way. It is a centre of our faith and devotion. We go there not to contest elections, but for its development,” Adityanath said.“I invite you to file your nomination from Ayodhya, and I will too, and try my luck there once. Let it be decided! The fight should be face-to-face,” he added.The challenge comes two days after Yadav dared the chief minister to contest from Ayodhya. The SP chief had claimed that the BJP was conducting surveys after his party announced its candidate but had failed to find a suitable nominee for the seat.Adityanath currently represents the Gorakhpur Urban assembly constituency. The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are expected to be held early next year.Yogi targets SP over Ayodhya’s developmentAdityanath also criticised the previous SP government over its handling of Ayodhya. He alleged that the temple town received only three to four hours of electricity and was littered with heaps of garbage during the party’s tenure.He further claimed that the SP government had imposed restrictions on Ramlila performances and erected barricades in the city.“The same Ayodhya is today writing a new chapter of development while giving shape to a new concept of Ram Rajya,” he said.The political exchange comes after the SP won the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat, which covers Ayodhya, in the 2024 general elections. SP candidate Awadhesh Prasad defeated the BJP’s Lallu Singh.Yogi accuses SP of dynastic politicsAt the Balrampur event, Adityanath accused the SP of misgovernance, protecting criminals and failing to provide employment opportunities to young people.“The SP is the party that sold the state and left it in a decrepid condition. That is why I say the real meaning of 'PDA' is 'Pradesh Dubao Alliance' (sink-the-state alliance),” he said.The chief minister was referring to Yadav’s political slogan, PDA, which stands for pichhde, Dalit and alpsankhyak, or backward classes, Dalits and minorities.Adityanath also accused the SP of dynastic politics. He alleged that the party had failed to give adequate representation to Dalits and backward communities in its Rajya Sabha nominations.He claimed that one of the two seats won by the SP had gone to party leader Ram Gopal Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav’s uncle, while the other had been given to a wealthy businessman. The SP also nominated industrialist and sports administrator Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani to the Rajya Sabha.CM highlights jobs and developmentAdityanath also accused successive governments led by the Bahujan Samaj Party and the SP of failing to complete a bridge at Mathura Ghat in Balrampur. He claimed that work progressed only after the BJP came to power.The chief minister said his government had provided government jobs to 9.5 lakh young people over the past nine-and-a-half years. He also pledged that Balrampur would not be left behind in development.Adityanath said his government had established a system to provide assistance and compensation to families affected by disasters within 24 hours. He added that steps were being taken to ensure prompt compensation in cases of human-wildlife conflict.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: For a champion who has conquered the biggest stages in para badminton, the prospect of carrying the Indian flag as the flagbearer at the upcoming Para Asian Games for Pramod Bhagat is still an experience that stands apart from every medal and accolade.A gold medallist at the Tokyo Paralympics, Bhagat is preparing for his fifth Asian Para Games, carrying with him the experience of six medals, including two golds and four bronze. Yet, despite years of competing at the highest level, the responsibility of carrying the tricolour has brought a fresh sense of excitement.Bhagat recalled watching flag bearers lead the Indian contingent during his earlier appearances at the continental showpiece. The sight left a lasting impression on him, and now, as he prepares to take on that role himself, the feeling has become all the more meaningful.Having already won Paralympic gold, two Asian Games gold medals and the Padma Shri, Bhagat has experienced several defining moments in his sporting journey. However, he believes that the honour of being flag bearer cannot be compared with any of those achievements.“My expectation is gold, but it won't be easy,” he said, underlining the ambition that continues to drive him despite an already impressive medal collection.For Bhagat, longevity at the highest level has been built on the ability to adapt. Every edition of the Asian Para Games brings a different set of challenges, with opponents improving, preparations changing and the demands of the sport becoming more intense.“When you go to the second or third Asian Para Games, there is a difference of four years. A lot changes in four years. I try to learn from the past and move forward. I try to do my best, and I want to be successful,” he said.That approach has helped Bhagat remain a key figure in India's para badminton movement. His focus is not simply on defending his reputation but on finding ways to improve with every campaign. The target remains gold, but the process involves learning from previous performances, understanding the competition and making the most of his preparation.Beyond his personal ambitions, Bhagat is equally encouraged by the growing strength of Indian para badminton. With the sport attracting greater attention and Indian athletes making their presence felt internationally, expectations have risen.The goal, he said, is to push the country's medal count even higher.“We want to win more than 10 medals in the Para Asian Games,” Bhagat said, reflecting the confidence within the Indian contingent.The optimism is backed by a broader upward trend in India's para-sports performance. Bhagat pointed to the country's growing medal tally, noting that India had crossed the 100-medal mark at the previous Asian Para Games. For him, the progress is evidence of how sustained support, improved facilities and greater visibility can translate into results on the field.He believes the transformation has been particularly noticeable compared with the early days of his career, when govt assistance and public recognition for para badminton were more limited.Bhagat credited the government's growing involvement and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for taking a personal interest in para badminton, which he said had helped bring the sport greater recognition and publicity. That visibility, in turn, encouraged private organisations to come forward and support athletes.“When you get good support, and your equipment and training facilities improve, you perform well,” he said.The backing from both the government and the private sector, Bhagat believes, has helped create a stronger ecosystem for para athletes. Better equipment, improved training infrastructure and greater exposure have given players more opportunities to prepare and compete at the highest level. The rising medal count, he said, reflects the difference that such support can make.As India looks to build on its achievements at the continental level, Bhagat's campaign carries significance beyond the medals he hopes to win. He represents a generation of athletes who have benefited from a changing sporting environment while helping raise the profile of para badminton through their performances.For the veteran shuttler, though, the immediate task remains clear: prepare well, learn from experience and pursue gold. The flag-bearing honour has added another dimension to his campaign, giving him a responsibility that goes beyond his individual events.Bhagat knows that success will not come easily, but he is ready to embrace the challenge. And when he leads the Indian contingent with the tricolour in his hands, the moment will represent more than the achievements of a champion. articles.title: Dr. Phil lists his Beverly Hills estate for $67.5 million after buying it for $29.8 million in 2010; the 2.76-acre Mediterranean Revival compound has 16,079 square feet, a pool, tennis court and guesthouse
articles.summary: Dr.
articles.body: Dr. Phil McGraw and his wife, Robin McGraw, are putting their sprawling Beverly Hills estate on the market for $67.5 million, seeking more than twice what they paid for the property 16 years ago. The listing was first reported by Realtor.com, with additional details reported by realestate.com.au and supported by earlier Los Angeles Times coverage of the McGraw family’s Beverly Hills real estate holdings. The Mediterranean Revival compound, located in the Beverly Hills Post Office area, spans 2.76 acres and contains 16,079 square feet of living space. McGraw and Robin purchased the property for $29.8 million in 2010 and completed the residence in 2011 following a construction process that reportedly lasted seven years. The current listing is being handled by Billy Dolan of Carolwood Estates.Designed by architect Kevin Clark, the property was conceived as more than a conventional mansion. It functions as a private compound, with a main residence, a separate guesthouse and accommodations for staff. The estate also has eight bedrooms and more than 10 bathrooms, according to Realtor.com.Inside, the home leans heavily into a traditional Mediterranean aesthetic. Large windows and French doors bring natural light into the formal living spaces, while fireplaces, high ceilings and ornate architectural details add to its old-Hollywood character.The kitchen is fitted with Wolf and Miele appliances and includes a butler’s pantry, while an informal dining area opens toward the outdoor spaces. A wine cellar is another notable feature, with its entrance reached via a staircase finished with herringbone-patterned brickwork. The primary suite occupies a substantial private retreat of its own, with a sitting area, separate bathrooms and expansive wardrobe areas.Outside, the property takes on the feel of a private resort. A large swimming pool anchors the landscaped grounds, while the elevated setting offers views toward the Los Angeles skyline and surrounding mountains. There is also a clay tennis court and an entertainment pavilion, giving the estate substantial recreational space without leaving the property. A four-car garage and large motor court provide additional room for residents and guests.At $67.5 million, the asking price comes to roughly $4,198 per square foot. If the property sells close to its asking price, the headline difference from the couple’s 2010 purchase price would be $37.7 million. That figure, however, does not represent their actual profit because it excludes construction expenses, renovations, maintenance, taxes, financing and transaction costs.The Beverly Hills estate is only part of the McGraw family’s broader property portfolio. Their holdings have included a Calabasas mansion purchased for $6.6 million in 2011, another Beverly Hills property acquired for $10 million in 2020 and a Dallas mansion purchased in 2020.The latest listing also arrives after increased attention around McGraw’s media business. Merit Street Media, the television venture he launched, entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in 2025. The bankruptcy court subsequently rejected the Chapter 11 case and moved the company toward Chapter 7 liquidation, according to court records and reporting cited in the property coverage. For now, the Beverly Hills estate stands as one of the more substantial properties in McGraw’s portfolio, combining nearly three acres of land with a 16,000-plus-square-foot residence, guest and staff accommodations, a pool, wine cellar and private tennis court.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: In 2022, road base tests mixed recycled tire pieces with crushed concrete, and both small and medium tire blends showed significant rutting after 1,000 loading cycles
articles.summary: Discover how mixing recycled tire pieces with crushed concrete can impact road construction, as tests reveal challenges and opportunities for sustainable paving materials.
articles.body: Worn out tires reach the end of their useful lives in huge numbers each year, and finding a second use for them is not easy. Researchers in Australia have been exploring whether old tires could go into road construction instead of landfill. Roads are often considered a practical target because they can take in large volumes of material. After testing by the Australian Road Research Board (ARRB), Victoria's transport department has been increasing the use of recycled materials in unbound bases for lightly trafficked state roads. Researchers at Melbourne's Swinburne University of Technology explored what happens when the two wastes are joined. Crushed concrete mixed with small and medium tire fragments showed significant rutting after 1,000 loading cycles in the wheel tracker test.What the team testedThe idea was to see if tire pieces could replace part of the quarry stone that normally forms the subbase layers of the pavement. The mixes contained recycled concrete aggregate (crushed demolition concrete) and tire derived aggregate (shredded pieces of old tires) in small and medium sizes. Two tests were made. The repeated load triaxial test squeezes a cylinder of material inside a pressurised cell again and again to measure permanent deformation. The wheel tracker rolls a loaded wheel back and forth over a compacted sample to measure rut depth. According to the paper, the triaxial test put samples through 30,000 cycles in three stages of 10,000, at a confining pressure of 50 kilopascals.Rutting is important because it is the groove that develops along wheel paths. Engineers trace it to too much deformation in the base layer, since the asphalt on top simply follows whatever moves underneath. A base settles under traffic, and eventually a rut appears on the surface. The Australian Road Research Board runs an oversized wheel tracker called Austrack, which applies heavy vehicle loads to predict how unbound bases will rut in the field. It is the sort of test any new base material must eventually pass.What the tests suggestedIn the wheel tracker test, the researchers recorded significant rutting in both blends after 1,000 cycles. The rut depth under the medium tire blend was higher than under the small tire blend for the first 760 cycles, after which the pattern changed. Overall, medium tire sections performed better, with less permanent deformation in the triaxial test and less rutting in the wheel tracker. The medium mix also resisted repeated loading better than the small one at a 2 per cent tire share. Crushed concrete alone deformed far less in the triaxial test than either tire combination.The results look discouraging for tire rich layers, yet the researchers still say the blends suit pavement base and subbase use, because the particle size, compaction, bearing strength and triaxial tests supported adding modest amounts of tire pieces. That gap makes sense once you consider where the material goes. A subbase sits below the base and carries less stress, so a small amount of tire in that layer is very different from a tire rich surface exposed to heavy wheels.Why rubber alters the blendEarlier work had not examined such a long horizon, so in 2019 researchers at RMIT University's Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering department blended crushed concrete with 0.5, 1 and 2 per cent crumb rubber and ran 100,000 loading cycles in a triaxial rig. Researchers from RMIT University’s Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering department blended crushed concrete with 0.5%, 1% and 2% crumb rubber, then ran 100,000 loading cycles in a triaxial rig in 2019, since earlier work had not examined such a long horizon.Tire pieces can go into road layers, but only in limited amounts, in medium rather than small pieces, and with the toughest tests done before anyone builds a road on them. Medium pieces performed better than small pieces, and plain recycled concrete performed better than either blend. The study suggests councils and contractors should be cautious, since a material can perform well in one test but struggle in another.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Suvendu eyes Bengal sweep: Can Mamata, Congress unite to challenge BJP?
articles.summary: In a bold statement following significant bypoll victories, West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari aims for a clean sweep in the upcoming 2029 Lok Sabha elections. This article explores the rising tensions in Bengal's political landscape and the possibility of opposition alliances against the BJP's growing influence.
articles.body: "We are set to win 42 out of 42 in the 2029 Lok Sabha election." West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari had made this grandiose claim even before the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll results. A visibly buoyant Adhikari reiterated the target after his party swept both seats. Victories in both constituencies were expected, yet the margins, particularly in Rejinagar, where roughly 70% of voters are Muslim, came as a revelation. With the all-important Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls likely to be held in late November, there is a perception that the BJP may win handsomely. It is up to the Opposition to put up a spirited fight.Bypolls have usually favoured the ruling partyWhat may give the Opposition some solace is the fact that bypolls, at least over the last decade or so, have followed an extremely predictable pattern in Bengal. Between the 2021 and 2026 Assembly elections, Trinamool won 20 of the 21 Assembly bypolls held in the state. Its dominance was particularly striking in 2024, when it swept all 12 by-elections, including four seats previously held by BJP legislators.In July 2024, Trinamool wrested Raiganj, Ranaghat Dakshin and Bagdah from the BJP despite the latter's electoral strength in these areas during the Lok Sabha election just weeks earlier. In November, TMC captured Madarihat, which the BJP had held since 2016. Even in June 2025, less than a year before its Assembly rout, Trinamool retained Kaliganj by more than 50,000 votes.There have been exceptions to the incumbent's advantage. In 2023, Congress, supported by the Left, defeated the ruling TMC in Sagardighi by nearly 23,000 votes. However, the MLA concerned, Bayron Biswas, soon joined TMC.Why BJP's victories still matterIn Nandigram, BJP's Hasi Rani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who had Mamata's support, by 1,22,753 votes. In Rejinagar, BJP's Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Aam Janata Unnayan Party candidate Golam Nabi Azad, son of party founder Humayun Kabir, by more than 75,000 votes.In both constituencies, BJP polled more votes than all its opponents combined. Rejinagar witnessed notable outreach from the CM, with Suvendu even saying that Muslims did not need to chant "Jai Shri Ram". He also urged them to turn over a new leaf and extend a hand of friendship to the new government.Following the result, Adhikari attributed BJP's success partly to support from beneficiaries of the Annapurna welfare scheme, under which eligible women receive ₹3,000 per month. Whether the BJP can really secure a share of the Muslim vote in elections with bigger stakes remains to be seen. But if it does, Suvendu's dream of a clean sweep in the Lok Sabha election may well look more realistic.Allegations of electoral excessesThe Opposition, though, has refused to grant legitimacy to the Assembly bypolls, citing alleged malpractices by the ruling machinery. Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar demanded fresh elections in both constituencies, alleging booth capturing, intimidation, bogus voting and the forcible removal of polling agents. AJUP, which had won the seat previously, alleged that its candidate received zero votes in 33 booths and just one vote in another 19 booths. Mamata's TMC faction made similar allegations of rigging, while the rival Trinamool faction and the Left also complained about polling agents being prevented from functioning.In Nandigram, Congress candidate Milan Pradhan alleged that party agents had been driven out of booths and voters prevented from voting. His earlier arrest in connection with an old case related to the Nandigram land movement had already prompted allegations of political harassment.BJP rejected the rigging allegations, maintaining that polling was peaceful. The Election Commission described voting as largely peaceful despite receiving complaints. One widely circulated claim that BJP had received more votes than the number of registered voters at a Rejinagar booth was subsequently rebutted by election officials, who said the original electorate figure was incorrect.Such allegations are not new to Bengal's electoral politics, one of the reasons why the opposition have frequently asked for central forces to conduct polls. The 2018 panchayat elections witnessed widespread reports of violence and intimidation. More than a third of the seats were won uncontested, overwhelmingly by Trinamool, amid allegations that opposition candidates had been prevented from filing nominations. A year later, the BJP increased its Lok Sabha tally in Bengal from two seats in 2014 to 18 in 2019.Political observers have linked that breakthrough partly to resentment over the conduct of the panchayat polls. Very recently, Abhishek Banerjee’s Diamond Harbour model of winning by record margin of votes had also come under scrutiny. For BJP though, barely a few months into power, the chances of pushback to any alleged excesses remain relatively modest.What's next for the Opposition?The INDIA bloc has upped the ante in the capital, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote manipulation during the SIR process. Leaders such as Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee and even those from the Left have been sharing the stage. With a common goal, the confluence is organic. But the state-level dynamics are very different, something that has affected the INDIA alliance for a long time.An INDIA alliance is unlikely to become a reality in Bengal, with Left and TMC cadres rarely seeing eye to eye. An alliance between Mamata's TMC and Congress remains an open question, with state leaders of the grand old party lukewarm about giving space to a leader who did not allow them much room to grow while in power.Mamata came to power in 2011 in alliance with Congress, but the two soon parted ways. Since then, the parties have hardly worked together politically, until this by-election. There have been several overtures from Congress in the past, but these were rebuffed by the then West Bengal CM, who wanted to maximise her political capital. Now that the script has flipped, Congress may not give in so easily.Former state Congress president Pradip Bhattacharya disclosed in September that the state leadership had advised against a proposed bypoll arrangement under which Congress would contest Nandigram and Mamata's Trinamool would fight Rejinagar. Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury's recent invitation to Mamata to return to Congress with her remaining MLAs and MPs came with a condition about leaving behind her political baggage, widely interpreted as a reference to Abhishek Banerjee.Even the Nandigram understanding was not a formal seat-sharing arrangement. Mamata supported Milan Pradhan after her faction's candidate withdrew. In Rejinagar, both parties contested separately. Many Congress leaders believe that it is time to rebuild the party in the state when opposition space is up for grabs. The BJP is still getting to grips with governance, and teething troubles in several areas, including the rollout of government schemes, have made headlines.The organisational crisis within Trinamool adds another dimension. Following the Assembly defeat, the party split into rival factions, prompting the Election Commission to temporarily freeze its original name and symbol. The Mamata-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led Democratic Trinamool Congress contested under different identities in the bypolls. Neither performed well. In Rejinagar, Mamata's faction received 3,847 votes, while Democratic Trinamool polled 2,044.The Left, meanwhile, continues to face the challenge of translating political visibility into electoral support. Younger leaders such as Satarup Ghosh, Dipshita Dhar and Srijan Bhattacharya have attracted attention, particularly on social media, but the party's electoral recovery remains limited.There were, however, modest improvements in the latest bypolls. In Nandigram, the CPI's Santi Gopal Giri increased his tally from 2,997 votes in May to 5,779. Congress also improved its vote count in both constituencies, although the Nandigram comparison is complicated by Mamata's support for its candidate.Municipal elections: The next big battleThe immediate electoral focus now shifts to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls, where voting is tentatively expected in late November. The stakes extend far beyond the two Assembly bypolls.In the 2021 Kolkata Municipal Corporation election, Trinamool won 134 of 144 wards, securing more than 72% of the votes. BJP won just three wards and Congress two. Interestingly, the Left Front, with nearly 12% of the vote, finished ahead of BJP in vote share despite winning fewer seatstThe forthcoming election will also be fought on a substantially altered map. Kolkata's wards have increased from 144 to 209, and Howrah's from 50 to 68. For both factions of TMC, this election will be the first major test of who enjoys greater public support. For Mamata Banerjee, south Kolkata remains her pocket borough, and following the humiliating defeat in Bhabanipur, she would be desperate to turn around her fortunes. For Firhad Hakim and others, it will be an opportunity to prove that they can win on their own without Didi's support.Congress and the Left have long been marginal forces in both Kolkata and Howrah, barring a few pockets. The Left appears inclined to contest independently in several areas, although the CPM has encouraged local discussions with Congress. Some Congress district leaders, meanwhile, have argued that the party should contest all 209 Kolkata wards on its own.The decisions are yet to be finalised, leaving Congress with a difficult choice between rebuilding independently, cooperating with the Left and exploring an understanding with Mamata.Road to 2029Nationally, Rahul Gandhi's success in rallying different INDIA bloc parties in the campaign demanding the resignation of the CEC has done his popularity no harm. The bonhomie between Sonia Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee at the recent press conference was there for everyone to see. They have maintained cordial personal relations despite the ebbs and flows in their political exchanges. But the political calculations in Bengal remain very different. Rahul's pointed attacks on Trinamool over corruption during the Assembly campaign had reinforced the Congress's adversarial position in the state. For local Congress workers, a sudden statewide alliance with Mamata would require a significant political adjustment. Didi however, remains in the frontlines in the protest against Election Commission and was detained on Saturday even as Rahul Gandhi skipped the protest and went to Chennai.At the same time, Mamata faces one of the most difficult phases of her political career, while the BJP confronts increasingly coordinated opposition protests at the national level. Hence the political equations could well change. After the municipal elections in Kolkata and Howrah, polls in more than 100 other civic bodies are expected next year, followed by panchayat polls in 2028 and the Lok Sabha election in 2029. Those who have power in the grassroots are likely to have a headstart in the Lok Sabha election.Suvendu has already set his sights on winning all 42 Lok Sabha seats in Bengal. Such a result would have significant implications for the BJP's national parliamentary tally. For Congress, the calculation is therefore not confined to the revival of its Bengal organisation. Its leadership must also consider the wider political ramifications of allowing the BJP a free-run in the state.For the Opposition, national unity over electoral issues is one thing. Building an effective political arrangement in Bengal is quite another. The coming municipal elections will provide the first major opportunity to see whether those differences can be bridged.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2024, Bangladesh tested a road made with shredded plastic bags and bottles; during a heat wave, it showed no visible cracking, while other roads showed visible distress
articles.summary: Bangladesh tests plastic-modified asphalt roads that withstand extreme heat, showing no cracks unlike conventional roads. Discover how recycled plastic could revolutionize road construction in hot climates.
articles.body: In a hot country, a new road never gets to enjoy its youth. Bitumen is the black binder that glues stone and sand together in asphalt. It softens as temperatures go up, and in high heat it can melt. When heavy traffic, humid air, and monsoon rain are added, cracks and potholes tend to follow soon after a fresh surface is laid. A Dhaka Tribune report noted that roads in Bangladesh's subtropical climate can develop cracks and potholes relatively quickly.April 2024 highlighted the strain caused by extreme heat. The Bangladesh Red Crescent Society, citing Bangladesh Meteorological Department data, reported 24 heatwave days in April, surpassing the previous April record of 23 days in 2019. Temperatures reached 42°C, 16°C above the annual average, and heat-related school closures affected 33 million children, according to Save the Children.One route stood out in Dhaka during that period. Civil engineer Sahadat Hossain of the University of Texas at Arlington said the plastic-modified road showed no visible signs of cracking or distress during the heatwave, while other roads in Bangladesh showed visible cracking and distress. The result still leaves questions about how the road was built, what else was measured and how much confidence the outcome deserves.Manufacture of the plastic roadAsphalt is a mix of stones, sand and bitumen. The Texas and Bangladesh teams replaced around 8% to 10% of the bitumen with melted plastic from everyday products, including single-use bags and bottles. The plastic is cleaned, crushed into small flakes and mixed into the asphalt at high temperatures so it melts and binds with the mix.Hossain compares the concept to putting rebar in concrete. It also reduces the amount of petroleum-based bitumen required. The same research program has also been tested in Texas. In a separate project near Dallas, about 4.5 tons of plastic waste was incorporated into nearly a mile of one-lane pavement.What the Dhaka tests foundThe Dhaka road is a 300-meter pavement at Rayer Bazar constructed in August 2023 and divided into four 75-meter sections, including one conventional control section, according to a 2026 ASCE conference paper. A study from the American Society of Civil Engineers details how the sections blended distinct plastic-modified asphalt and aggregate base layers. Researchers tested them with a lightweight deflectometer, a portable gadget that analyzes how much a pavement flexes when a weight is dumped on it.The plastic sections had a dynamic deflection modulus more than 50% higher than the conventional section. The best performance was achieved by a plastic modified asphalt surface on a cement treated base utilizing plastic aggregate.A later PhD project at the same university tracked the Dhaka road and a second site in Cumilla for three years. The Dhaka mix had 8% high-density polyethylene, while the Cumilla mix contained 8% low density polyethylene and 0.5% polypropylene. Stiffness in the plastic sections decreased more slowly than in the conventional sections. Ride quality showed a similar pattern. After three years, the International Roughness Index increased by 29% on the conventional pavement, while it decreased by 3% to 11% on the plastic-modified sections, according to the 2026 UTA dissertation.What remains unclearThe cracking comparison was a visual assessment made against several roads across Bangladesh rather than one nearby strip, so it is better viewed as an encouraging sign than as a controlled outcome. A pending US patent application for the pavement technology lists Sahadat Hossain, Tanvir Imtiaz and Tahsina Islam as inventors.Not every city has a consistent supply of clean, sorted plastic. Scaling up the feedstock remains a challenge. Microplastic release remains a separate environmental question. A 2024 study in Resources, Conservation and Recycling estimated that microplastic release from recycled-plastic asphalt could be about three orders of magnitude lower than the release of rubber particles from tire wear, while noting that the potential environmental impact still requires assessment.The Dhaka trial showed promising early pavement performance during extreme heat, while later stiffness and ride-quality measurements also favored the plastic-modified sections. Its value still needs to be demonstrated over decades and at the scale of a national road network.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Russian president Vladimir Putin and US president Donald Trump held a “very substantive and friendly” conversation on Friday, with neither leader wanting
articles.body: Russian president Vladimir Putin and US president Donald Trump held a “very substantive and friendly” conversation on Friday, with neither leader wanting to end the call first, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said on Saturday.The remarks came as a proposed Russian diesel deal with Washington drew sharp criticism from Kyiv amid renewed Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities.Russian news agency Interfax quoted Ushakov as saying on Saturday that the conversation lasted an hour and a half.“Neither wanted to be the first to hang up,” Ushakov said. “They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time.”The Kremlin said the leaders spent most of the conversation discussing efforts to end the war in Ukraine. Putin, however, played down the prospects of resuming three-way peace talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in the near future.The conversation came a day after Trump announced an agreement under which Russia would supply diesel to the US and global markets, with the stated aim of easing fuel prices.The announcement also involved a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian fuel, prompting concern in Kyiv that Moscow could benefit financially while continuing its military campaign.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the move, calling it a “weak decision” and “an investment in a war that must be ended”.His criticism intensified on Saturday after Russian strikes killed at least 17 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, including three children, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service. At least 18 people were wounded after Russian aerial bombs struck residential buildings.“Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy wrote on X.He said the attacks showed Moscow interpreted “any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities”.“Russia’s choice is war,” Zelenskyy said in a later Telegram post, following drone attacks on energy facilities and a ballistic missile strike on Kyiv. Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said four people were wounded in the daytime attack on the Ukrainian capital.Zelenskyy urged Washington, European countries and other partners to maintain pressure on Moscow, warning that additional export revenue would help fund weapons components, drone upgrades, missile production and the recruitment of mercenaries.Western sanctions were imposed after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Efforts to end the war have stalled, partly over Moscow’s demands for four Ukrainian regions it does not fully control.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Stage set for Sunday showdown: CJP to march again tomorrow; traffic advisory issued
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced another march to Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Sunday a day after an unprecedented security clampdown and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced another march to Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Sunday a day after an unprecedented security clampdown and mass detentions thwarted its planned demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory warning commuters of possible disruptions across several key roads and intersections in the national capital.In a post on X, the CJP said the government feared the consequences of people uniting against it but asserted that the organisation would not back down.The fresh call for mobilisation comes after more than 7,000 protesters were detained across Delhi on Saturday, according to police sources, cited by news agency PTI. Those detained included CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, former chief ministers, opposition leaders, student activists, lawyers and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.Despite heavy security deployment, barricades and restrictions on movement across central Delhi, some groups of protesters attempted to reach the designated protest site. Incidents of stone-pelting and clashes with security personnel were also reported at multiple locations.The developments have triggered a sharp political confrontation, with opposition leaders accusing the government of suppressing dissent and the BJP defending the police action. With the CJP announcing another march, authorities have warned that traffic movement could be affected across several parts of the capital on Sunday. Delhi Traffic Police issues advisoryThe Delhi Traffic Police said traffic could be affected on October 11 in view of the prevailing law-and-order situation. Diversions will be enforced from 6am, depending on the situation on the ground.Commuters have been advised to account for possible delays while travelling through central Delhi and other affected stretches. The advisory lists 30 intersections, flyovers and road junctions where movement could be disrupted.The affected locations include:Jantar Mantar and central Delhi: Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Outer Circle Connaught Place-Sansad Marg T-point, Tolstoy-Janpath crossing and Mandi House roundabout.Connaught Place and adjoining areas: Outer Circle Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road T-point, Chemsford Road-Outer Circle Connaught Place T-point, Guru Nanak Chowk, Jhandewalan roundabout and Panchkuian roundabout.Key road junctions and flyovers: Dhaula Kuan flyover, Lodhi Road flyover, Moti Bagh flyover, Bhikaji Cama Place underpass, Neela Gumbad roundabout and Sardar Patel Marg-Panchsheel Marg crossing.Other affected stretches: Shankar Road-Vande Mataram T-point, Windsor Palace roundabout, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk roundabout, RML Hospital roundabout and Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg junction.The police said the diversions would depend on the prevailing circumstances. Motorists travelling through these areas should check official traffic updates and allow additional time for their journeys.What happened in Delhi on Saturday?Delhi witnessed an extensive security operation on Saturday as police moved to prevent the CJP's proposed demonstration. More than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed, barricades were erected across Lutyens' Delhi and security checks were intensified at several locations. Jantar Mantar remained largely deserted as protesters were prevented from reaching the site.CJP leaders Abhijit Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained inside an aircraft shortly after it landed in Delhi from Mumbai. Rathee was detained from his residence in Gurugram's Sector 56. In a pre-recorded video released after his detention, Dipke said CJP organiser Ajinkya Shinde would lead the protest.Several opposition leaders were also detained while attempting to join the demonstration. They included AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar. Left leaders, student activists, lawyers and other protesters were picked up from multiple locations.Tensions escalated in the afternoon when protesters allegedly hurled stones at security personnel near Akashwani Bhawan and Hanuman Temple in Connaught Place. Police personnel were injured in the incidents, while officers moved to disperse the crowds and detain those involved.Opposition leaders condemned the crackdown. Banerjee described the situation as a “Super Emergency”, while Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of turning the “mother of democracy” into a “muzzled democracy”. Rahul Gandhi urged young people to continue protesting against what he alleged were attacks on democratic institutions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2015, volunteers removing litter from an Irish beach spotted an unknown prehistoric shell midden, adding a newly recorded archaeological site to Sligo’s coastline
articles.summary: In a remarkable find during a beach clean in County Sligo, Ireland, volunteers uncovered a prehistoric shell midden, adding to the region's archaeological significance. This discovery highlights the risks posed by coastal erosion to ancient sites.
articles.body: A routine beach clean is usually measured in bags of plastic, bottles and other debris removed from the sand. But in May 2015, a group of volunteers on Ireland’s County Sligo coast came across something far older. While clearing litter at Rosses Point, Martina Butler noticed a thin, unusual layer of oyster shells exposed along the edge of a dune.According to the MASC Project, the discovery initially appeared out of place among the modern rubbish. The shells were later identified as a possible prehistoric midden, a refuse deposit left by people who gathered and ate shellfish. The find mattered not only for its archaeological value, but also because a member of the public spotted it without formal archaeological training.A shell layer hidden beneath the dunesButler was participating in a beach clean-up organised by the North West Sea Kayaking Association under the 'Clean Coasts' initiative. It was on 15 May 2015 that Butler observed this distinctive shell layer along with burnt material in the darker sediment layer underneath. She had previously seen middens elsewhere on the Sligo coast, so she suspected this feature could also be archaeological. She took photographs of the site and then notified the Monitoring the Archaeology of Sligo’s Coastline, or MASC, project the next day. This mattered because shell deposits on beaches are not always archaeological in origin. Waves have been known to gather the shells at the high-tide mark, while fires on the beach create artificial charcoal and stones.A member of MASC visited the site, recorded its GPS coordinates and photographed the visible remains. The dense collection of oyster and periwinkle shells, along with charcoal in the deposit, strengthened the case that people had used the site. The Archaeological Survey of Ireland also checked it out. Eleven days after the discovery by Butler, it was registered as an archaeological monument under RMP No. SL008-203.What the midden revealedThe newly uncovered midden is small. Its deposit is about 6.5 metres long and 1.2 metres in width, while its depth varies from just a few millimetres to about 10 centimetres. It is composed mainly of oysters, along with some periwinkles, stones and charcoal. For archaeologists, such waste can provide information about how the coast was used in the past. Middens are food waste deposits that can reveal what people collected and ate. Shell types, charcoal, and other waste can be used by scientists to study the ways the coast was utilised and whether there was repeated or brief settlement.Research on shell middens has shown how these deposits can preserve evidence of long-term relationships between coastal communities and marine resources. Work published in the Journal of Archaeological Science has demonstrated the value of analysing shell assemblages and their surrounding deposits to reconstruct past human use of coastal environments. The Sligo find could not be dated precisely. According to the researchers at MASC, middens in Ireland can range from the Mesolithic Era, circa 8,000-4,500 BC, all the way up until later periods. However, the thin layer of material at the Rosses Point site may indicate a brief, possibly seasonal occupation.When erosion uncovers the pastHowever, the discovery also came with a risk. The erosion of the dunes that uncovered the site was also putting it at risk. The deposit lay beneath dune sand on a harder stone surface. Tides and storms in 2014 and 2015 eroded the dune and exposed the archaeology. For example, the MASC Project was created because erosion and storms kept revealing archaeological sites along the Sligo coast. In 2015, it was reported that there were 148 sites at risk of archaeological monuments located only 10 meters away from the coast, where five new monuments not previously identified were discovered through citizen science.The findings of later archaeology in Sligo have further confirmed the fragility of such coastal deposits. Shell middens have been recorded as being exposed in eroding cliffs and dunes, with some sites containing shell, faunal bone, charcoal, and fire-cracked rocks. The researchers have warned that any future storms could remove archaeological evidence before it is recorded. Butler’s discovery was not only an unusual beach-cleaning find; it also showed how people using the coastline can act as extra eyes for archaeologists.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Solar farms in France restored native wildflowers and proved beneficial for bees and butterflies, proving to scientists what everyone believed wrong, not all pollinating plants kill insects or ...
articles.summary: French solar farms are bringing back native wildflowers.
articles.body: ​French solar farms are bringing back native wildflowers. The findings also showed that these sites can support bees and butterflies, challenging the notion that solar farms uniformly harm pollinating insects and the plants they depend on. Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Those changes can include shifts in temperature, moisture, and vegetation, and research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions.​An article in the journal Biological Conservation examined the effects of solar panels on plant-pollinator interactions at 20 solar farms in Southern France. The study found that plants under the panels had 76-86% fewer pollinator visits than plants outside them. But the impact varied across the farm.​Researchers found that “inter-row” plants, which grow between rows of solar panels, continued to attract bees, butterflies and other pollinators. Their numbers were lower than in areas outside the solar farms, but the difference was less pronounced than in areas under constant shade.​Shade changes the way plants and insects interact​The researchers found that much of this variation was linked to how much shade the panels cast. Plants in continuous shade attracted fewer visits, but plants in partial shade between rows of panels still attracted pollinators. We found more pollinator activity in the sunnier spots.​The researchers suspect the pattern may be partly due to the cooler conditions produced by solar panels. Pollinators tend to avoid cooler and shaded areas, creating what the study calls different “microclimates” around the panels.​Shade can also affect the plants themselves. Reduced sunlight can decrease plant diversity and the quantity of pollen and nectar flowers produce. This means that even when pollinators do visit plants growing under panels, these plants may provide fewer resources.​The research also examines whether the panels themselves may affect insect movement. The research suggests that solar installations may serve as “a physical barrier” for butterflies that respond strongly to changes in their environment. Changes in soil moisture under the solar panels may also affect plant growth and insect feeding.​Solar farms could still benefit native plants​The findings do not mean solar farms are inherently harmful to pollinators. Instead, they show that conditions within the same solar installation can vary depending on panel placement, vegetation and land management.​The researchers also discovered something unexpected about land maintenance. Grazing led to lower pollinator abundance than mowing, the opposite of what the scientists expected.​As Europe continues expanding solar power, researchers want future studies to examine pollinator behaviour in greater detail, including differences between individual species. More data could help scientists understand how solar panels alter local microclimates and how those changes affect pollination.​The broader question is how solar farms can be designed and managed to become “pollinator-friendly” while avoiding a “net loss of pollinator biodiversity.” The French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform, leaving room to explore how native vegetation and better land management could make these energy sites more compatible with bees, butterflies and other insects.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Look forward to welcoming you to Jerusalem’: Israeli prez pens letter to hero pilot captain Smit
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has written to Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, wishing him a speedy recovery and expressing his desire to welcome him
articles.body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has written to Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, wishing him a speedy recovery and expressing his desire to welcome him to Jerusalem, where he will personally present him with Israel’s highest civilian honour for heroism.In a post on X on Saturday, Herzog said he had conveyed his prayers for Machchhar’s recovery in a letter the pilot received over the weekend. Machchhar is recovering in a hospital in Abu Dhabi after sustaining serious injuries in an attack by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30.“Captain Smit Machchhar, you are a hero of Israel, India, and all of humanity. In my letter to you, which you received over the weekend, I shared our prayers for your full and speedy recovery. As I wrote in my letter, I look forward to welcoming you to Jerusalem once you regain your strength. On behalf of the people of Israel, I would be honored to present you with Israel’s highest recognition of civilian heroism, the Israeli Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism,” Herzog wrote.The announcement follows Herzog’s decision to honour Machchhar for his role in averting a potential aviation disaster aboard flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 passengers.The co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe inside the cockpit and attempted to take control of the aircraft. Despite suffering serious injuries, the Indian pilot managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to overpower the attacker. The aircraft subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.Herzog announced the award while honouring six Israeli passengers in Jerusalem for their role in thwarting the alleged hijacking attempt. He credited their courage and presence of mind with helping save 174 lives.Machchhar underwent surgery following the incident and is recovering in Abu Dhabi. Ministry of external affairs said earlier this week that his condition was improving and he was responding well to treatment.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had also spoken to Machchhar during his recovery, praising his courage and inviting him and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to participate in Israel’s Independence Day celebrations.You use AI every day. articles.title: Several wounded in Riyadh airport attack, operations suspended, Saudi aviation authority says
articles.summary: RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that fo...
articles.body:
RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the ‌country's civil aviation authority said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, but it comes amid ‌an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia.

The airport had already been struck in two earlier attacks this week that left four ​people dead and exposed vulnerabilities in the kingdom's ability to defend itself as it wages war on the Houthis. Saudi Arabia's early warning system did not issue an alert ahead of Saturday's incident.

The Saudi government's media office did not immediately respond to questions from Reuters.

One eyewitness at the airport on Saturday reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. ‌More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing ⁠towards the facility.

An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.

US TO "LOOK AT" JOINING SAUDI FIGHT AGAINST ⁠HOUTHIS: TRUMP

Following the attack, US President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, was asked whether the United States planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.

"We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, ​so we'll ​make a decision. We move very quickly," he said.

The US embassy ​in Riyadh said it was "aware of attacks" and "strongly ‌recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas."

The UK and Irish embassies in Saudi Arabia said in statements on X that they were also aware of a "serious incident" at the airport. The Canadian embassy said that "ongoing military activity" had impacted operations at the airport.

Flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point.

Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and ‌from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the ​closure of Riyadh airport because of the "security situation" there.

Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways ​earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs ​and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday.

Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week ‌had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend ​or cancel services to the ​Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host major energy and investment conferences.

Organisers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.

The Houthis have said ​airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it ‌a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier ​this month.

(Reporting by Timour Azhari in Riyadh; Additional reporting by Steve Holland in Washington DC; Writing by Enas ​Alashray and Maya Gebeily;Editing by Gareth Jones and Joe Bavier)
